name: getrlimit
synopsis: int setrlimit(int resource, const struct rlimit *rlim);
int prlimit(pid_t pid, int resource, const struct rlimit *_Nullable new_limit, struct rlimit *_Nullable old_limit);
description: The getrlimit() and setrlimit() system calls retrieve and set resource limits for a process. Each resource has a soft limit, which the kernel enforces, and a hard limit, which acts as a ceiling for the soft limit and can only be raised by privileged processes.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: The resource to get or set limits for, such as RLIMIT_AS or RLIMIT_CPU.

parameters.name: rlim
parameters.description: Pointer to a rlimit structure containing the soft and hard limits.

parameters.name: pid
parameters.description: The process ID for which to get or set limits (for prlimit).

parameters.name: new_limit
parameters.description: Pointer to a new rlimit structure to set limits (for prlimit, can be NULL).

parameters.name: old_limit
parameters.description: Pointer to a rlimit structure to store the old limits (for prlimit, can be NULL).

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: A pointer argument points to a location outside the accessible address space.
The value specified in resource is not valid; or, for setrlimit() or prlimit(): rlim->rlim_cur was greater than rlim->rlim_max.
An unprivileged process tried to raise the hard limit; the CAP_SYS_RESOURCE capability is required to do this.
The caller tried to increase the hard RLIMIT_NOFILE limit above the maximum defined by /proc/sys/fs/nr_open.
(prlimit()) The calling process did not have permission to set limits for the process specified by pid.
Could not find a process with the ID specified in pid.

versions: Linux-specific; prlimit requires _GNU_SOURCE; RLIMIT_NICE since Linux 2.6.12
examples: printf("Previous limits: soft=%jd; hard=%jd\n", (intmax_t) old.rlim_cur, (intmax_t) old.rlim_max);
printf("New limits: soft=%jd; hard=%jd\n", (intmax_t) old.rlim_cur, (intmax_t) old.rlim_max);
